10.title: Click-to-plant garden that grows over time
10.visualRubric: A strong frame shows a lit garden plot with a clearly readable ground, sky and a camera angle that shows the whole plot, with 15+ plants at mixed growth stages. Score each 1-5. (1) Composition and readability: ground, horizon and plot fully visible, plants distributed where clicked, nothing clipped or black. (2) Plant form and growth legibility: sprouts, mid-growth and mature plants are clearly distinguishable, with leaves and flowers rather than bare primitives. (3) Colour and variation: varied flower colours and sizes with a harmonious palette, not uniform. (4) Lighting and grounding: directional light, soft shadows or contact shading so plants sit on the ground, with sensible exposure. (5) UI polish: counter and Clear button legible, unobtrusive and styled, not overlapping the garden focus.
10.probe: Page-level, no framework knowledge needed. (1) Wait for window.__TASK_STATE__.ready === true; take frame A of #app. (2) Call window.__plantAt(-3,0), (3,2), (0,-3), (2,-2), (-2,3) and also dispatch real mouse clicks at three canvas positions (e.g. 30%/70%, 50%/80%, 70%/65% of canvas size); assert plantCount increases by the expected number (8) and DOM text matches 'Plants: 8'. (3) Capture frames at t=0.5s, 4s and 9s after planting; assert plants[i].growth is monotonically non-decreasing and reaches >= 0.95 by 9s, and that the mean absolute pixel difference between the 0.5s and 9s frames exceeds a threshold (about 2% of pixels changed) in the plant region. (4) Click the DOM element containing 'Clear' and assert plantCount === 0. (5) Click a canvas pixel above the horizon and assert plantCount is unchanged. Record the final frame for the visual judge. A solution fails the probe if __TASK_STATE__ is missing, counts are wrong, or growth does not change.

11.title: Solar-system explorer with focus on click
11.visualRubric: A strong frame shows a cinematic, readable solar system. Score each 1-5. (1) Composition and scale readability: overview shows the full system with a good camera angle, orbits legible, planets neither microscopic nor overlapping, nothing clipped. (2) Planet and star rendering: distinct planet colours and surface variation, a convincing glowing star (emissive or bloom), a clear ring and moon. (3) Lighting: planets lit from the star with visible day/night shading, not flat uniform fills. (4) Background and depth: dense starfield with depth cues, orbit lines subtle and not dominating. (5) Focus view and UI polish: focused planet fills a good fraction of the frame, the info panel is legible, well placed and styled, and the Pause button is clear.
11.probe: Page-level, no framework knowledge needed. (1) Wait for __TASK_STATE__.ready; capture overview frame A; assert planets.length >= 6. (2) Capture frames 1s apart and assert pixel difference above a threshold, and assert planet positions in __TASK_STATE__ change between samples with the inner planet's angular displacement (around the star's position or origin) larger than the outer's. (3) Click the Pause button, record positions, wait 1.5s, assert positions are unchanged (within 1e-3) and the button text is 'Play'; click again to resume and assert positions change. (4) Call window.__focusPlanet('<name of 3rd planet>') and also, separately, click the canvas at the projected screen position of a planet (derive from the frame or a pixel search); wait 2.5s; assert focused equals that planet name, cameraDistanceToFocus is below 25% of the overview camera distance, the info panel DOM text contains the planet name and two numbers, and that the planet is still near screen centre 2s later (follow). (5) Press Escape and assert focused === null, panel hidden, and the frame matches overview framing (full system visible). Save the overview and focus frames for the visual judge.
